final_answer: Turbine T-4 suffered the pilot's only significant failure when its bearing seal corroded through, allowing seawater into the nacelle—the root cause was corrosion of the bearing seal housing. Over 24 months, the pilot delivered 18.7 GWh to the grid, 6% below the 19.9 GWh forecast. The project finished at EUR 41.25 million against a EUR 36.7 million budget—an overrun of EUR 4.55 million (12.4%), driven mainly by the T-4 repair campaign. Environmental monitoring found no statistically significant impact on fish migration patterns (p = 0.41). Lead engineer Dr. Ines Marchetti recommended replacing titanium fasteners with duplex stainless steel on all remaining nacelles, a change accepted in principle by the steering group. The steering group ultimately approved Phase 2 for Q3 2026, contingent on completing the bearing seal redesign and passing a successful dry-dock endurance test.
